verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The two displayed identities are stated verbatim as two lemmas, with the paper's weights and signs: moment 2 (angularRadialViscosity f) = 0 unfolds to ∫ r²(f'' + f'/r − f/r²) dr = 0 (the v-line) and moment 1 (axialRadialViscosity f) = 0 to ∫ r(f'' + f'/r) dr = 0 (the γ-line). Two rewritings: (i) Lean's `moment` integrates over all of ℝ, the paper over R > 0 — for the shell-supported profiles of Proposition 8.4 these coincide by `positive_radialMoment` (IntegratedMeanBalances.lean:826, proved from `positive_integral_eq_integral`, line 224, for support ⊆ Icc a b with 0 < a); (ii) Lean's hypothesis is smoothness plus compact support rather than shell support, so the division by r at r = 0 (a junk value in Lean) is neutralised almost everywhere by `weighted_angular_viscosity_ae` / `weighted_axial_viscosity_ae` (lines 166, 173). The paper's middle member (2 − 1 − 1)∫v dR is not displayed as a term; the same accounting is produced in the Lean proofs by two applications of `moment_deriv_succ` followed by `linarith` (lines 206–209, 220–222), and for the γ-line Lean cancels ∫ r f'' against ∫ f' exactly as the paper cancels −∫γ_R + ∫γ_R. Both lemmas are the ones actually invoked in the Proposition 8.4 chain, at IntegratedMeanBalances.lean:666 (`integrated_angular_balance`) and :702 (`integrated_axial_balance`).
